audit.whatIsWrong: Every level row was set to Skill even though the prose says Graves wins level 1 outright, Akshan owns level 3, and Graves owns 6 onward. Packet chart reads Graves/Skill/Akshan/Skill/Graves/Graves/Graves.
audit.why: A flat Skill chart hides the only two things a player needs from this lane: the level-1 all-in and the level-3 kite window.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Graves (7/10), Level 3 Akshan (4/10), Level 6 through 2+ items Graves (7/10); levels 2 and 4-5 stay Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes carried no cooldowns and described 'two E charges' for Akshan.
audit.why: Heroic Swing has no charges — it is a single 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s cast. Comeuppance is 100/85/70s. Those numbers are what make 'fight while it is down' actionable.
audit.corrected: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and it needs terrain to hook into; Comeuppance is 100s at rank 1. Graves' Collateral Damage is also 100s, so level 6 is ult-for-ult.
sources: _kits/akshan.json E cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and text, R cd 100/85/70

audit.whatIsWrong: MAJOR: Akshan's kit was described using Graves' own ability. Five places said Akshan 'weaves autos so his Quickdraw refreshes' — Quickdraw is Graves' E. Akshan's Q was called 'Q powder bursts'; it is Avengerang, a boomerang. Smoke Screen was called a blind.
audit.why: Data Dragon: Akshan P is Dirty Fighting (every third hit shields him and adds a reduced-damage extra attack), Q is Avengerang (extends range on each enemy hit), E is Heroic Swing (grapples into terrain). Graves' W reduces sight range — it does not cause attacks to miss.
audit.corrected: What he actually gains from weaving autos is Dirty Fighting: every third hit bonus-damages you and shields him, so a long poke exchange arms him. Heroic Swing must hook terrain, so in the open lane he has no escape — and Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure it hits, so standing behind your wave eats it outright.

audit.why: Wave advice already tells you to hold near the middle and shove with a destination, which is right against a champion whose escape depends on nearby terrain.

edits.before: Akshan is a squishy ranged skirmisher, so at Level 1 you actually win the all-in: walk up, accept one Q tick, and unload your full two-shell spread point-blank — your stacking True Grit resists eat his return damage and he has no swing terrain to grapple away with in an open lane. The catch is Levels 2-3, where his second E charge comes online and he starts kiting your reload windows, weaving autos so Quickdraw refreshes and poking your health bar from a range your shells can't reach. Don't burn E chasing a dash you can't catch; sit on your charges, last-hit at Q range, and wait for him to step into your face.
edits.after: Akshan is a squishy ranged skirmisher, so at Level 1 you win the all-in: walk up, accept one Avengerang, and unload the full two-shell spread point-blank — True Grit eats his return damage and Heroic Swing has no terrain to hook in an open lane. The catch is Level 3, where he starts kiting your reload, letting Dirty Fighting shield him on every third hit and poking with a boomerang that gains range each time it clips something. Don't burn Quickdraw chasing an 18-second swing you can't catch; sit on it, last-hit at Q range, and wait for him to step into your face.

edits.before: Once you hit 6 the lane flips back to you. His whole game is opening distance with the E dash, but Collateral Damage closes it instantly — bait the dash, R him as he commits, then W-smoke the autos he wants to kite back with and finish with your shell spread. Through Levels 4-5 keep your E charges for the chase, not the engage. He's paper-thin; one clean R into auto-into-Q combo deletes him, and your W blind shuts off the autos that fuel his Quickdraw refresh and passive marks.
edits.after: Once you hit 6 the lane flips back to you. His whole game is opening distance with Heroic Swing, but Collateral Damage closes it instantly — bait the swing, R him as he commits, then Smoke Screen the ground he retreats over and finish with your shell spread. Through Levels 4-5 keep Quickdraw for the chase, not the engage. He's paper-thin; one clean R into auto into Q deletes him. His Comeuppance stops on the first minion it hits, so answer it by standing inside your wave, not by running.

notes: MAJOR CROSS-CHAMPION CONTAMINATION FOUND: five lines described Akshan as refreshing 'Quickdraw' — that is Graves' own E, not anything in Akshan's kit. All corrected to Dirty Fighting (his real three-hit shield passive). 'Q powder bursts' also corrected to Avengerang, and 'two E charges' removed — Heroic Swing has no charges, it is one 18s cast that requires terrain to hook. Packet defects list was empty, so none of this was caught automatically. Only 23 Emerald+ games in the packet, so I leaned on the kit text and the existing prose, not the 56.52% win rate.
